v1.feedback: The vascular→soap tonal flip is a genuine concept, but it lands as a shader uniform ramp on a single differential-growth ring — the form never actually branches or reads as vascular, so the 'surprise' is just a color change on a lumpy rising tube. Make the transition structural: hollow the tube walls, fragment the mesh into bubble-thin patches that separate and drift, so the form itself lightens — not just the material. The thin-film interference function is too uniform across the surface; vary thickness per-vertex using curvature or age so the iridescence pools in concavities like real soap film, and clamp the palette to 2-3 dominant hues instead of full-spectrum rainbow to keep it restrained.

v2.feedback: The thin-film shader is decorative sinusoidal color mixing, not actual interference — replacing the three-color sin/cos blend with a proper optical-path-difference → spectral lookup (even a cheap 1D ramp texture indexed by 2·n·d·cosθ/λ) would sell the bubble iridescence far more convincingly. The bubble inflation wave is a nice structural swerve but the radius change is too subtle at default camera distance; push the inflated sections to 2–3× base radius so the silhouette shift is unmistakable in the first two seconds. Consider dropping fogDensity to ~0.025 so the upper tower (where the bubble wave arrives) isn't eaten by fog before the payoff lands.
